findings.defect: The whole convexity block is the textbook monotone-LCP dictionary applied to prop:lcp, which the paper already owns; each of the four is three to four lines from prop:lcp plus the q_v display the paper prints immediately after thm:transport-objective. THE THREE LINES for vr:hessian and vr:convexity: (1) in prop:lcp's notation at base beta = 0, z_v w_v = eps_v^2 (y_v - f_{v,0}(y))(y_v - f_{v,1}(y)) = q_v, so the route's q IS the LCP complementarity gap z^T w = z^T(Mz+q); (2) prop:lcp says y -> z is an affine bijection and M = E R_1 R_0^{-1} E, so the Hessian of q in y is the congruence R_0^T (EME) R_0 symmetrised, i.e. B = sym(R_0^T R_1); (3) a quadratic is convex iff its Hessian is PSD and congruence preserves PSD, so B >= 0 iff M + M^T >= 0, and polarisation ab = ((a+b)/2)^2 - ((a-b)/2)^2 applied rowwise is the 'difference of two energies'. THE THREE LINES for vr:optdir: (1) prop:lcp(b) says the complementary basic solution at S = beta xor pi is the image of y_pi, with w_v = 0 on S and z_v = 0 off S; (2) hence (z-z')_v (w-w')_v = 0 unless v is in S sym-diff S' = {v : pi(v) != pi'(v)}; (3) (z-z')^T(w-w') = d^T B d with d = y_{pi'} - y_pi, and its nonnegativity is exactly monotonicity of M. The route attributes the underlying equivalence (Cottle-Pang-Stone) in prior_art but still reports these as results of class new-object/new-relation.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex l.8035 prop:lcp (M = E(I-Q_bar-beta)(I-Q_beta)^{-1}E, P-matrix, complementary basic solutions = y_pi, free variable sign = s_C); l.14254, the paragraph after thm:transport-objective, which prints q_v(x) = (x(v)-x(v^(0)))(x(v)-x(v^(1))) = 0 and calls the branch among 2^{|C|} of them 'the difficulty'; def:lasserre-two builds its relaxation on the same q_v.

findings.defect: R is exactly the handicap-zero slice of the LCP route the paper surveys and closes in rem:lcp. rem:lcp records that interior-point methods solve LCP(M,q) in O((1+kappa) sqrt(n) L) iterations for a sufficient matrix of handicap kappa; the handicap of a sufficient matrix is 0 precisely when M is positive semidefinite, so on R the bound rem:lcp cites is already polynomial. The route's stated GAP ('convex quadratic programming is in P', Kozlov-Tarasov-Khachiyan) therefore misidentifies what is missing: the algorithmic half of R was already surveyed and set aside by the paper as 'not ours and closed', and no fifth import of a different kind is needed to see that R is polynomial modulo prior art. What is actually missing is content for R, not an algorithm for it.
findings.evidence: frontier.tex l.14395-14413 rem:lcp: 'interior-point methods solve LCP(M,q) in O((1+kappa) sqrt n L) iterations when M is sufficient with handicap kappa, so a polynomially bounded handicap would decide prob:main. We do not develop this, because it is not ours and it is closed.'

verdict:
VERDICT: new-theorem, but only on the narrowest possible reading, and the headline as written is not supportable. Two results survive independent scrutiny; the four that carry the headline are the textbook monotone-LCP dictionary applied to an object the paper already owns.

1. DID THE ROUTE CHANGE THE OBJECT? No. The object is prop:lcp's matrix M written in the paper's own harmonic normal form and symmetrised: B = sym((I-P_0)^T(I-P_1)) is the congruence R_0^T (EME) R_0, and the "energy" q is the LCP complementarity gap z^T w, i.e. the sum of the very forms q_v the paper prints after thm:transport-objective and builds def:lasserre-two on. The collapse to prop:lcp IS proved (that is what vr:convexity(b)<=>(d) says), which rule 0 of this round grants as a result -- but it is a proved collapse onto a route the paper explicitly surveyed and closed in rem:lcp, and the route presents it as an equivalence theorem rather than as a collapse. The first-passage data (P_0, P_1, Delta = P_1 - P_0) is also not new: Delta's rows are exactly def:signdef's vectors d^v, so the "new" spectral condition ||Delta (I - Pbar)^{-1}||_2 <= 2 is a norm bound on the paper's own sign-definiteness data. The second object, reversibility, IS new to the paper -- and the route proves it is unusable.

2. WHAT IS ACTUALLY NEW. (a) CVX4 (48 vertices, 3 Max) and CVX6 (127 vertices, 4 Max): two nondegenerate one-player stopping games with B strictly positive definite -- handicap zero -- whose all-switches runs have length 4 and 6, attaining h*_1(3) and h*_1(4). I rebuilt both from the game files with my own exact solver and every stated number is right (stopping, T w* = w*, the exact minors, zero ties, the runs, the switch sets, the outmaps, dyadic denominators 2^5 and 2^7, full reachability). Since the paper's own realisation of the SAME orientation (0,1,3,6,7,4,5,2), the 58-vertex game of rem:blowup-measured, has det B < 0 (I recomputed it), one AUSO has both a handicap-zero and a positive-handicap realisation: monotonicity of the LCP is not a property of the improvement orientation and imposes no bound on the bottom-antipodal height at m <= 4. That is a genuine, if narrow, contribution to the question rem:auso-size and the paragraph after prop:seven-k1 pose, "which such matrices occur". (b) vr:rev-trivial: profile-reversibility forces the non-sink edge relation to be symmetric, every component to be a path, and every component to carry at most one controlled vertex -- a correct proof (I checked all three steps, including the sink-successor case in (b) and the self-loop case in (c)) and a legitimate door-closing collapse.

3. IS IT CIRCULAR OR VACUOUS? Not circular -- vr:variational's objective is computable from the instance with no profile named, which is a real difference from thm:transport-objective's 2^{|C|} linear objectives. But the class R is vacuous by this round's own test: it has no verified member outside the trivially tractable regime. Every listed member is either |C| = 1 (H_m, G_8, S, S_r -- so their membership is the route's own clause (a) and says nothing), |C| = 2 (WD, CC), or one-player with |C| = Theta(N) (the ladder, RC(k)); the only two-player members are |C| <= 3. And R is algorithmically vacuous relative to the paper: it is exactly the handicap-zero slice on which rem:lcp's cited interior-point bound O((1+kappa) sqrt(n) L) is already polynomial -- the paper's "closed and not ours" route -- so naming R as a tenth class would add a class the paper cannot prove polynomial by its own means and cannot show contains anything it does not already solve.

4. THE REAL REMAINING GAP, stated more precisely than the route states it: not "convex quadratic programming is in P" (rem:lcp already records an interior-point bound that is polynomial at handicap zero, and declines to import it), but -- does R contain a stopping game whose subgame reachable from v_0 lies outside all nine of the paper's tractable classes, i.e. is R anything more than a poly-time-decidable label on games the paper already solves?

5. INTEGRATION: MIXED -- integrating the LaTeX as submitted would make the paper WORSE; integrating two extracts would make it slightly BETTER. WORTH INTEGRATING: (i) vr:convex-long and vr:ceiling, as one proposition with the two normal forms, placed in the paragraph after prop:seven-k1 that already says "the handicap of rem:lcp is no constraint either" and phrased in the paper's own vocabulary (handicap zero / M + M^T positive semidefinite), not under a new class name -- it strictly extends that paragraph from the cyclic two-player game to the tall one-player runs, and adds the one-AUSO-two-realisations point; both games verified here. (ii) Five lines of vr:convexity as a REMARK in the same place: B = sym(R_0^T R_1) is invariant under relabelling a vertex's two actions, so "positive definite at its all-zero base" may be replaced by "at every base" without computation, which is the principal-pivot invariance rem:lcp already cites -- this repairs a genuinely loose phrase in the paper and should carry that attribution. (iii) vr:rev-trivial as a short remark, with vr:rev-vacuous compressed to one sentence pointing at lem:splice(a). NOT WORTH INTEGRATING: vr:hessian, vr:variational and vr:optdir as theorems (restatements of prop:lcp plus attributed textbook LCP theory, and vr:optdir is additionally inert on a class where the problem is convex anyway); the class R under a name (no content, no algorithm within the four imports, a tenth class the paper would have to caveat twice); vr:content's membership tables (trivial where they are not already printed); and the word "energy", which collides with thm:energy.
